one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: (1) TSMC September sales on Oct 8 and its Q3 call on Oct 15 (src 30). August was +53% y/y and N2 has 4x the tape-outs of N3 (src 28, 29), so I expect a supportive read on design demand. (2) Cadence Q3, very likely after the close on Oct 26. Correction from round 1: that date is an aggregator estimate (src 35, 43), not company-confirmed. Cadence issued its Q2 webcast notice three weeks before the print (src 42) and has issued none for Q3 yet, so there is a small chance the print falls just outside the window. The guide is $1.595-1.625B revenue and $2.01-2.07 EPS; Zacks consensus is $2.04 and $1.61B (src 40), right at the midpoint. Backlog is a record $8.1B (src 1, 22). Peers read strong: Synopsys guided FY27 +15% (src 3) and Siemens EDA grew >30% (src 18). A beat is likely and largely expected. (3) FOMC on Oct 28: Polymarket has 74% hold / 26% +25bp on $21.4M volume, with the 10y at 5.29% (src 45, 46). The September 19% drawdown came with no company news as yields rose, so a hike is a real downside risk to the multiple. (4) The stock is up ~28% in 12 sessions, including +6.2% on 10/1 in sympathy with Synopsys (src 20). Reversal risk roughly offsets post-earnings drift. Net: median at spot, sigma ~12.5% (41%/3.5 = 11.7% plus a little for the print and FOMC), symmetric. Unchanged in substance from round 1, because none of the corrections changes the balance of short-horizon risk.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (70%): NTM non-GAAP EPS at the horizon ~$10.65 (0.25 x FY27 consensus ~$9.55 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$11.03) x 34x = $362, and FCF yield (30%): NTM FCF at the horizon ~$2.44B at a 2.8% yield = EV $87.1B, less ~$1.0B net debt, over 276M diluted shares = $312. Blended ~$347.

0.25 x $9.55 + 0.75 x $11.03 = $10.66. This matches the supervisor's reconciled figure, which I adopt because it rests on the broader consensus.

The stock is at ~36.7x FY27 Zacks ($350.73/$9.55) and its 5-year average is ~44x (src 34). Synopsys is at ~25x FY27 ($475.70/$19.08, src 20, 3). The 10y at 5.29% (src 45) argues against re-rating toward history. I keep 34x: a discount to Cadence's history for the AI-agent overhang and high rates, and a premium to Synopsys for margin and execution.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at horizon ~$2.44B / 2.8% = EV $87.1B; less net debt ~$1.0B; / 276M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $2.48B notes less $1.44B cash, held roughly flat because guided buybacks absorb most FCF (remaining authorisation $1.0B, src 16). The supervisor's $0.5-1.0B range is consistent with this; I keep the conservative end.
The FY26 diluted share guide is 275.5-277.5M (Q2 CFO commentary, src 1), and 275.4M were outstanding at 6/30 (src 16). Buybacks offset SBC.

FY26 FCF ~$1.85B (OCF $2.0B less ~$0.15B capex, src 1), grown ~17%/yr: FY27 $2.16B, FY28 $2.53B. The NTM blend (0.25/0.75) is $2.44B, about $8.85 per share. The growth rate is in line with consensus EPS growth (src 39) and below Synopsys' mid-20s FCF CAGR (src 3).

Synopsys: ~$3.1B FY27 FCF (src 44) against ~$88B market value at $475.70 (src 20) is ~3.5% on equity, or ~3.2% on EV including its Ansys debt. A yield consistent with my 34x P/E would be ~2.5% (FCF/share $8.85 / EPS $10.65 / 34). My round-1 3.1% implicitly used a ~27x multiple, which was inconsistent, as the supervisor noted. I use 2.8%, between the P/E-consistent 2.5% and Synopsys' 3.2% EV yield, because Synopsys is now guiding faster growth (+15% vs Cadence ~+13% consensus, src 39) and that caps the premium.

bear.story: Agentic or open-source AI flows (Kimi K3 demo; ChipAgents $134M, Cognichip, Ricursive $300M) start pressuring seat pricing, or the hyperscaler capex debate ($1.3T in 2027 on thin FCF) triggers a design-spend pause that hits hardware and IP. The FY27 guide in Feb comes in conservative, as FY26's did (11-13% organic). Rates stay above 5%, and the Affiliates Rule suspension lapses on Jan 10, 2027, hitting China (15% of revenue). NTM EPS ~$10.4 at ~24x, Synopsys' multiple.

base.story: The industry keeps compounding at mid-teens: Synopsys FY27 +15%, Siemens EDA >30%, ESDA +12.7%, TSMC N2 tape-outs 4x N3. Cadence delivers about consensus (FY27 ~$9.55 on ~+13% revenue; NTM ~$10.65 at the horizon). The multiple holds at ~34-35x while agent monetisation stays a narrative, not a number.

bull.story: Custom silicon (Broadcom and Marvell XPU rosters) and 2027 hyperscaler capex drive record hardware, IP and SD&A. Cadence's subscription-plus-consumption agent pricing starts showing up in bookings, and the Feb guide beats consensus. Yields ease. NTM EPS ~$11.2 re-rates toward ~43x, near the 5-year average.

thesis_break_reason: $250 is about 5% below the 52-week low ($262.75, 2026-02-03) and ~9% below the no-news, rate-driven September low ($273.96 on 9/15). At NTM EPS of ~$10.65 it implies ~23.5x, at or below Synopsys' ~25x despite Cadence's higher margins and record $8.1B backlog. Since a sentiment and yield shock alone stopped near $274, a trade at $250 would most likely mean fundamental damage: an FY27 guide well below ~13% growth, backlog shrinking, Synopsys or Siemens flagging price pressure, real commercial adoption of agentic or open-source flows at advanced nodes, or loss of China access after the Affiliates Rule suspension ends on Jan 10, 2027. I lowered this from $255 because the NTM EPS base fell, keeping the same ~23.5x anchor. I stay slightly above the supervisor's $245 because a 23x multiple on consensus EPS already sits below the peer floor.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor (new sources 39-47) corrected three of my inputs, and 8 follow-up searches and fetches confirmed each one. (a) FY27 EPS: Zacks has $9.43 with revenue $7.13B, +12.9% (src 39). The StockAnalysis free page no longer shows FY27, but the supervisor read $9.56 there. My WallStreetZen $9.76 was the high outlier, so NTM at the horizon is ~$10.65, not $11.0. (b) The Q3 date is an aggregator estimate (src 43); Cadence's Q2 notice came three weeks ahead (src 42) and no Q3 notice exists. (c) China: CM Trade Law confirms the Affiliates Rule is suspended, not repealed, to Jan 10, 2027 (src 41), so the risk is deferred. My industry evidence stands and the supervisor rated it strong: Siemens EDA >30%, TSMC Aug +53% and N2 4x tape-outs, Synopsys FY27 +15% and ~$3.1B FCF (src 18, 28, 29, 3, 44), plus startup funding (src 24, 25). The ESD Alliance Q2 2026 report is still not out (Q1 was +12.7%, src 10). Valuation: P/E $362 (NTM $10.65 x 34x). I accept the supervisor's point that my FCF leg was internally inconsistent: 3.1% implied ~27x. I re-based it to NTM FCF at the horizon and a 2.8% yield, giving $312, which is still below the P/E leg because Synopsys now guides faster growth at a ~3.2% EV FCF yield. Weights 0.7/0.3 give $347, vs $355 in round 1 and the supervisor's $358. I stay below the supervisor's figure because I do not accept a 2.4-2.5% FCF yield while the faster-growing peer trades at ~3.2-3.5% and the 10y is 5.29%. Scenarios $250/$368/$480 at 25/50/25 give a mean of ~$367. The ladder is 90% lognormal (median $360, sigma 0.31) plus 10% bear-tail lognormal (median $250, sigma 0.35), for an overall median of ~$350, about spot. Sigma stays below the 41% realized vol, since that was inflated by one-off narrative and rate shocks that the tail and scenarios carry. Compared with round 1, the upper strikes are trimmed slightly (K=421: 0.298 to 0.283) and the lower strikes are about unchanged. The 1-month ladder is unchanged in substance, with the FOMC added and the date caveat.
